summary: As of mid-2026, the LLM landscape is dominated by OpenAI's ChatGPT/GPT-5 family with roughly 54-56% of global AI web traffic, followed by Google Gemini at 25-28% and Anthropic's Claude at 9-13%. The market has consolidated around a handful of major proprietary players while open-source models like Meta Llama 4, DeepSeek-V4, and Qwen3 have seen explosive developer adoption, with 79% of developers now using open-source LLMs according to Mozilla/SlashData surveys. Enterprise aggregator platforms (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx) significantly amplify real-world consumption beyond direct-API numbers, particularly for Claude, Llama, and Mistral.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.1
models.popularity_notes: Commands 53-56% of global AI chatbot web traffic (Similarweb, mid-2026), leads LLM API market via OpenAI API plus massive reach through Azure OpenAI Service on Microsoft's enterprise cloud, making it the single most consumed LLM by both consumer and enterprise volume.
strengths: Largest consumer and enterprise install base globally
Strongest brand recognition and ecosystem integrations
Available on Azure OpenAI giving Fortune 500 enterprise reach
Broad multimodal capabilities including vision and code
Extensive plugin and tool-use ecosystem
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise and consumer applications requiring broad capability and maximum ecosystem support

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Holds 25-28% of global AI chatbot web traffic with visits growing ~450% year-over-year to 2.9 billion in May 2026 (Similarweb), and benefits from deep integration into Google Workspace, Android, and Google Vertex AI enterprise platform.
strengths: Industry-leading 1M token context window
Native Google Workspace and Search integration
Available on Google Vertex AI for enterprise deployments
Strong multimodal performance across text, image, video, and audio
Rapid year-over-year traffic growth indicating accelerating adoption
models.best_for: Long-document analysis, multimodal enterprise workflows, and Google ecosystem-integrated applications

models.name: Claude Opus 5 / Claude Fable 5.1
models.popularity_notes: Holds 9-13% of global web traffic with 855% year-over-year growth to 952M visits in May 2026, and critically leads enterprise API spending at 40% share (Menlo Ventures 2025), with broad availability on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI amplifying enterprise reach far beyond direct API numbers.
strengths: Leads enterprise API spending at 40% share among large organizations
Available on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI for secure enterprise use
Top scores on reasoning and safety benchmarks
Preferred model for regulated industries requiring responsible AI
Claude Fable 5.1 tops Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 66
models.best_for: Enterprise applications requiring high reliability, safety, and compliance, especially legal, finance, and healthcare

models.name: Meta Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: The most downloaded open-weight model family on HuggingFace with millions of pulls, adopted by 79% of open-source LLM users per Mozilla/SlashData, and available on every major aggregator including AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx, giving it unmatched distribution breadth for a free model.
strengths: Free to download and self-host with permissive commercial license
Available across all major cloud aggregators (AWS, Azure, GCP, IBM)
Massive HuggingFace community with fine-tuned variants
Strong general reasoning as the top open-weight model for that task
Enables on-premise deployment for data-sensitive enterprise environments
models.best_for: Self-hosted enterprise deployments, fine-tuning for domain-specific tasks, and cost-sensitive production workloads

models.name: DeepSeek-V4 / DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.popularity_notes: Captured 4.1% of global chatbot web traffic and 24.4% of text requests on OpenRouter in the week of September 21, 2026, with V4-Pro ranking as the top open-source model for bug fixing and code generation on the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard (July 2026), driving outsized developer adoption relative to its age.
strengths: Top-ranked open-source model for code generation and bug fixing
Exceptional cost efficiency — developed with limited hardware investment
24.4% of OpenRouter API traffic showing massive developer-facing demand
Strong reasoning capabilities rivaling closed proprietary models
Available via API and self-hosted, giving flexibility for all deployment types
models.best_for: Code generation, debugging, and cost-efficient reasoning tasks where open-source flexibility is required

models.name: Grok-3 / Grok-4
models.popularity_notes: Holds 2.4% of global AI chatbot web visits (May 2026, Similarweb via Momentic) with distribution advantage from native X/Twitter platform integration giving access to hundreds of millions of social media users, and growing API adoption among developers attracted to its real-time information capabilities.
strengths: Native integration with X platform providing real-time web data access
Strong performance on math and reasoning benchmarks
Witty conversational style differentiating it in consumer use cases
Rapidly growing model family with regular capability updates
Growing enterprise API interest following Grok-4 release
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval, social media analytics, and applications requiring up-to-date web knowledge

models.name: Qwen3 / Qwen3-235B
models.popularity_notes: Adopted by over 90,000 enterprises across consumer electronics, gaming, and other sectors, with Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking redefining the open-weights landscape with trillion-parameter scale and support for 119 languages, making it the dominant model for Asian-market enterprise deployments and multilingual applications.
strengths: Adopted by 90,000+ enterprises with strong Asian market penetration
Best-in-class multilingual support covering 119 languages
Qwen3-235B offers trillion-parameter scale as open-weight model
Available in multiple sizes from efficient small models to massive MoE variants
Strong HuggingFace download numbers and active open-source community
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise applications, Asian-market deployments, and organizations needing large-scale open-weight models

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.popularity_notes: Available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx giving it strong enterprise aggregator coverage, recognized as the top open-source model for speed and efficiency per kairntech 2026 rankings, with Mixtral MoE variants showing strong HuggingFace download momentum.
strengths: Available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx
Best open-source model for speed and inference efficiency
Mixture-of-Experts architecture delivers strong performance per compute dollar
European AI provider preferred for GDPR-sensitive deployments
Broad aggregator coverage amplifies enterprise adoption beyond direct API
models.best_for: Latency-sensitive production APIs, European compliance-required deployments, and cost-efficient enterprise inference

models.name: Microsoft Copilot (GPT-5 backend)
models.popularity_notes: Holds 1.3% of global AI chatbot web visits but this dramatically understates adoption since it is embedded in Microsoft 365 reaching over 400 million commercial Office seats, Windows 11, GitHub Copilot, Bing, and Azure OpenAI Service — giving it the broadest enterprise surface area of any AI product by seat count.
models.cost_input: Bundled in M365 subscription or Azure consumption pricing
models.cost_output: Bundled in M365 subscription or Azure consumption pricing
strengths: Embedded in Microsoft 365 with 400M+ commercial user potential
GitHub Copilot is the most-used AI coding assistant by developers
No separate API needed for organizations already on Azure/M365
Seamless integration with Word, Excel, Teams, and Outlook workflows
Enterprise security and compliance inherited from Microsoft cloud infrastructure
models.best_for: Microsoft-ecosystem enterprises seeking AI embedded directly into existing Office, GitHub, and Azure workflows

models.name: Perplexity AI
models.popularity_notes: Holds 1.3% of global AI chatbot web visits (May 2026, Similarweb) with a distinctive search-augmented architecture that has driven rapid developer and prosumer adoption, particularly among researchers and knowledge workers who need cited, real-time web-grounded answers.
strengths: Native real-time web search grounding with automatic citations
Rapidly growing prosumer and researcher user base
Sonar API allows developers to embed search-augmented LLM in products
Competitive web-visit share placing it on par with Microsoft Copilot
Lower hallucination risk for factual queries due to retrieval architecture
models.best_for: Research assistants, knowledge management tools, and any application requiring real-time cited web information
